title: AI is creating a new wave of philanthropists. The system they’re walking into is broken
excerpt: Sometime in the near future, a significant portion of the people building today's AI industry are expected to become very rich.
content_html:
Nick Allardice, David Goldberg

Sat, August 15, 2026 at 8:30 AM EDT 4 min read

Sometime in the near future, a significant portion of the people building today's AI industry are expected to become very rich. Many are already thinking about what to do with that wealth. 

The two of us advise some of the most philanthropically motivated people in tech. These are people who genuinely want, and have the means, to make a real difference. But the current infrastructure around giving large amounts of money away is widening the gap between intention and action. 

In 2010, some of the wealthiest people in the world signed the Giving Pledge – a public commitment to donate the majority of their fortunes to charitable causes. It was heralded as a turning point for American philanthropy. But more than a decade on, follow-through looks underwhelming. 

We believe the reason for that runs deeper than any single giving vehicle. The incoming wave of philanthropists is different to the last, but they will meet the same infrastructure and incentives. 

For many, the moment of liquidity itself can be disorienting. The stakes feel enormous while the philanthropic landscape feels overwhelming. Lawyers, financial advisors, and colleagues all have opinions. Some would-be donors retreat back into work and let the moment pass. Others give to the first credible organisation that shows up with a compelling pitch. And the infrastructure most donors encounter at that moment is not designed to help them do better.

The answer most of these newly wealthy philanthropists will arrive at, the answer the financial industry is already prepared to offer, is a donor-advised fund (DAF). The mechanics of a DAF are relatively simple: open an account, transfer your pre-IPO equity before the tax window closes, take the deduction, and punt the decision on where to give until later. Later can mean 12 months, 12 years, or never, and the system's incentives quietly favor the last option. Opening a DAF feels like the responsible move and, in many ways, it is. But it also means joining a system that, despite its good intentions, has developed a serious structural problem, one that a new wave of philanthropists could make significantly larger.

There is currently over $300 billion of philanthropic capital sitting in American DAF accounts. That figure alone is striking, but the more telling number is what's happening to it: only around a quarter of DAF assets are paid out in any given year, a substantial portion of which simply goes from one DAF to another without helping any beneficiaries and with no legal obligation to distribute anything at all. In 2024, the most successful charitable fundraiser in the United States was not a hospital, a food bank, or an international relief organization. It was Fidelity Charitable, a DAF sponsor that took in nearly $16 billion in contributions. Eleven of America's top twenty fundraising "charities" are DAF sponsors. The money is piling into DAFs but it is not moving out.

content_html_zh:
尼克·阿勒迪斯、大卫·戈德堡

2026 年 8 月 15 日星期六，美国东部时间上午 8:30 阅读 4 分钟

在不久的将来，当今人工智能行业的建设者中很大一部分预计将变得非常富有。 许多人已经在考虑如何处理这些财富。

我们两人为科技界一些最具慈善动机的人士提供建议。 这些人真正想要并且有能力做出真正的改变。 但目前围绕捐赠大量资金的基础设施正在扩大意图与行动之间的差距。

2010年，世界上一些最富有的人签署了捐赠誓言——公开承诺将其大部分财富捐赠给慈善事业。 这被誉为美国慈善事业的转折点。 但十多年过去了，后续行动看起来平淡无奇。

我们相信，其原因比任何单一的捐赠工具都更为深刻。 即将到来的慈善家浪潮与上一波有所不同，但他们将满足相同的基础设施和激励措施。

对于许多人来说，流动性本身可能会让人迷失方向。 赌注巨大，而慈善事业却让人感觉势不可挡。 律师、财务顾问和同事都有意见。 一些潜在的捐助者退回工作岗位，让这一刻过去。 其他人则向第一个以令人信服的宣传方式出现的可信组织捐款。 大多数捐助者当时遇到的基础设施并不是为了帮助他们做得更好而设计的。

大多数这些新富慈善家都会得出的答案，金融业已经准备好提供的答案，就是捐赠者建议基金（DAF）。 DAF 的机制相对简单：开设一个账户，在税务窗口关闭之前转移您的 IPO 前股权，进行扣除，然后再决定在哪里给予。 稍后可能意味着 12 个月、12 年，或者永远不会，系统的激励措施悄悄地倾向于最后一个选项。 开设 DAF 感觉像是一个负责任的举动，从很多方面来说，确实如此。 但这也意味着加入一个尽管初衷良好但已经出现严重结构性问题的体系，而新一波慈善家可能会使这个问题变得更加严重。

目前美国 DAF 账户中有超过 3000 亿美元的慈善资金。 这个数字本身就很惊人，但更能说明问题的是它所发生的事情：在任何一年中，只有大约四分之一的 DAF 资产得到支付，其中很大一部分只是从一个 DAF 转移到另一个 DAF，没有帮助任何受益人，也没有分配任何东西的法律义务。 2024 年，美国最成功的慈善筹款活动不是医院、食品银行或国际救援组织。 DAF 的赞助商 Fidelity Charitable 接受了近 160 亿美元的捐款。 美国排名前 20 位的筹款“慈善机构”中有 11 个是 DAF 的赞助商。 资金不断涌入 DAF，但并未流出。
